# Overview

This document describes the intended end state of the TRA pipeline. The
pipeline starts from no data — a fresh project directory with no
downloaded filings and no firm list — and ends with a structured
database of every Tax Receivable Agreement disclosed on EDGAR, the
public companies that pertain to each one, and human-readable timelines
at both the firm level and the TRA level. The TRA-level timelines
explicitly track contracts as they move between companies via
acquisition, spin-off, beneficiary reassignment, or repurchase.

The pipeline is organized into five phases. Phases 1 through 4 run
end-to-end on the first build. Phase 5 is the incremental-refresh path
that runs on a schedule once the initial build is in place.

# Pipeline diagram

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["EDGAR full‑text search"] --> B["Phase 1<br/>Discovery and acquisition"]
    B --> C["data/tra‑mentions/"]
    C --> D["Phase 2<br/>Per‑firm reading"]
    D --> E["Phase 3<br/>Cross‑firm consolidation"]
    E --> F1["Phase 4a<br/>Firm timelines"]
    E --> F2["Phase 4b<br/>TRA timelines"]
    E --> F3["Phase 4c<br/>Structured tables"]
    F1 --> G["Phase 5<br/>Refresh"]
    F2 --> G
    F3 --> G
    G -.->|new filings| A
```

# Phase 1: Discovery and acquisition

**Goal:** discover every TRA-mentioning filing on EDGAR and download the
relevant documents into per-firm directories.

A single EDGAR full-text search step returns per-filing hits across the
variants of "Tax Receivable(s) Agreement(s)" or "TRA" (as a whole word),
grouped by the filer's CIK. The same step filters those hits to filings
within the form types we care about (8-K, 10-K, 10-Q, S-1, S-4,
prospectus variants, proxy statements) and downloads the relevant
documents per firm. For each filing, the step saves:

- The primary document (the 8-K body, the 10-K body, the registration
  statement body, etc.) so the per-firm reading agent in the next phase
  can understand the business context; what transaction was happening,
  who the parties were, and whether the TRA was being created, amended,
  terminated, or merely mentioned.
- Any EX-10.\* exhibits that mention TRAs in the body. Exhibits that do
  not mention TRAs are skipped.

Filings whose only TRA mention is from boilerplate language in a
separate contract (most commonly in debt agreements) are still
downloaded at this stage; the determination of whether a TRA exists
happens in Phase 2 when the agent reads the body.

The output is one directory per firm at
`data/tra-mentions/<firm-slug>/`, containing the firm's downloaded
filings indexed by accession number. The phase runs end-to-end on the
first build, then incrementally during Phase 5 refresh to catch new
firms and new filings since the previous run.

**Deliverable:** a populated `data/tra-mentions/` tree with one
subdirectory per discovered firm.

# Phase 2: Per-firm reading

**Goal:** for each firm, read its filings in chronological order and
write a narrative log that explains what happened with the TRA at this
company and classifies each filing's TRA exhibits by operative effect.

For every firm directory, a dedicated agent reads the firm's filings one
at a time, oldest first, and appends an entry to that firm's
`filing-log.md`. Each entry explains:

- What this filing was about — what transaction or disclosure prompted
  it.
- Why the TRA is mentioned — whether the firm is establishing, amending,
  terminating, repurchasing, settling, or merely referencing a TRA in
  passing.
- The firm's role with respect to the TRA — whether it is the obligor
  (PubCo), a beneficiary, an acquirer that has assumed someone else's
  TRA, a financing arm of an obligor, or a firm that mentioned a TRA
  without ever being a party to one.
- Which exhibits in this filing are themselves TRAs (original contracts,
  amendments, restatements, terminations, repurchases, settlements, or
  assignments) versus exhibits that merely reference TRAs.

Each firm's `filing-log.md` carries a YAML frontmatter section that
captures the firm-level summary (firm name, CIK, TRA relevance, TRA
role) plus a machine-readable table of every TRA exhibit discovered
across the firm's filings, with the operative-effect description for
each. The narrative explains the story; the frontmatter and table make
the file consumable by Phases 3 and 4.

This phase is where the agent does the work an automated regex
classifier cannot do: read the 8-K body to see what the transaction is,
follow the chronology across filings to understand whether a 2024
termination is unwinding a 2014 origination, recognize that an "Exchange
and Termination Agreement" attached to a merger 8-K is a TRA termination
even though its title does not contain the words "Tax Receivable
Agreement". Section 11 of `tra-background.md` documents the
substance-over-form rule that the agent applies.

The agent works sequentially by firm. The `filing-log.md` itself serves
as the agent's durable memory across long firm processing. When the
agent's context fills, prior filings' narrative entries are still in the
log and inform later decisions.

**Deliverable:** one `filing-log.md` per firm, with frontmatter,
narrative, and machine-readable exhibit table.

# Phase 3: Cross-firm consolidation

**Goal:** group TRAs across firms by underlying contract, so the same
contract appearing in multiple firms' filings is recognized as one
contract that has moved between parties.

A single TRA can appear under multiple CIKs over its lifetime, for
example:

- An originating PubCo files an original TRA in its IPO 8-K.
- When faced with a potential acquisition, PubCo amends the TRA to waive
  the Change of Control termination if the acquisition goes through
- After PubCo is acquired, the acquiror files the TRA as an exhibit
  following the closing of the merger.
- The TRA is later settled by the acquiror and a termination is filed.

Phase 3 walks all firms' `filing-log.md` files and groups TRA exhibits
by the underlying contract. Two exhibits represent the same contract
when their parties, effective date, payment terms, tax attributes, and
termination provisions all match (Section 9 of `tra-background.md`
carries the full criteria). When the agent's reading in Phase 2 already
established the cross-CIK link (e.g., "this is the same TRA that
originated at Acme PubCo and was assumed by BigCo at the 2024 merger"),
Phase 3 honors that link. When the link is ambiguous, the consolidation
step raises the case for manual review rather than guessing.

The output is a contract-level index: one entry per distinct original
TRA, listing all firms that have ever been parties to it, and all
exhibits across all firms that represent that contract in any state
(original, amended, restated, terminated).

**Deliverable:** a TRA index identifying every distinct contract and its
cross-firm document set.

# Phase 4: Output generation

**Goal:** produce the three end-user deliverables: per-firm timelines,
per-TRA timelines, and the structured database.

This phase reads the per-firm logs from Phase 2 and the cross-firm index
from Phase 3, then generates three outputs.

## Per-firm timelines

For each firm, a concise chronological summary of its TRA-related
activity: which TRAs it is party to, in what role, with what payment
activity, and how its position with respect to each TRA evolved. A firm
with one TRA that originated at IPO and remained in force gets a short
timeline; a firm that originated a TRA, was acquired, had the TRA
transferred to the acquirer, and later disclosed beneficiary-side
receipts gets a longer one.

The firm timeline answers: *what is this company's TRA story?*

## Per-TRA timelines

For each distinct TRA identified in Phase 3, a chronological summary of
the contract's lifecycle across all parties: origination, amendments,
restatements, beneficiary reassignments, acquirer assumption,
terminations or repurchases. When a TRA is transferred between firms (a
beneficiary is acquired, an obligor merges into another company), the
per-TRA timeline tracks the contract through the transition rather than
fragmenting it across the per-firm views.

The TRA timeline answers: *what is this contract's story?*

## Structured database

The same information rendered in structured tables for downstream
analytical use. The tables are append-friendly so Phase 5 refreshes can
extend them without rewriting history. The minimum set:

- A TRA-level table: one row per distinct TRA, with originator, current
  or final obligor, beneficiary identity (if known), key dates, current
  status, and the four standard contractual terms.
- An events table: one row per TRA event (origination, amendment,
  restatement, termination, repurchase, beneficiary change, acquirer
  assumption), with date and source-filing citation.
- A firm-TRA-role table: one row per (firm CIK, TRA id) pair, with the
  firm's role (PubCo, beneficiary, acquirer, financing arm,
  never-executed) and the date range over which it held that role.

**Deliverable:** per-firm timeline files, per-TRA timeline files, and
the structured database tables.

# Phase 5: Refresh

**Goal:** keep the database current as new filings appear on EDGAR over
time, without rebuilding from scratch.

The refresh path re-runs Phase 1 in incremental mode: query EDGAR for
filings filed since the previous run, identify any new firms that have
begun mentioning TRAs, download the new filings into the existing
per-firm directories. For firms with new filings, the Phase 2 reading
agent picks up where it left off; the existing `filing-log.md` provides
the firm's history, and the agent appends new entries for the new
filings only.

Phases 3 and 4 then re-run against the updated logs to refresh the
cross-firm index and the output files. When a refresh introduces a
new TRA-relevant event (a previously in-force TRA gets terminated, a new
firm becomes a TRA party for the first time), the timelines and database
tables update accordingly.

**Deliverable:** an updated database state reflecting all EDGAR activity
through the refresh date.

# Current implementation map

The conceptual pipeline above is the end state. This section shows what
exists in `scripts/` today (July 2026), which scripts call which, and in
what order they run.

Phase 1 is the only phase implemented as code: the
`scripts/phase1_discovery/` package, invoked as

```bash
PYTHONPATH=scripts pixi run python -m phase1_discovery --start 2001-01 --end 2026-05
```

Its driver runs four steps in sequence — discovery sweep, CIK registry,
per-firm acquisition, done marker — and every EDGAR request goes through
the shared `scripts/sec_edgar/` client layer (rate-limited, cached under
`.tra_history_cache/`). Phases 2 and 3 have no scripts yet; they will be
agent skills operating on the Phase 1 output tree. Phase 4d exists as a
pair of scripts that currently consume the older `TRA-contracts/`
summary files produced by the `tra-build-timeline` skill; they will be
repointed at the Phase 2/3 outputs as those land.

```{mermaid}

    subgraph P1["scripts/phase1_discovery/ — Phase 1, implemented"]
        DRV["driver.py — orchestrator<br/>python -m phase1_discovery"]
        DISC["discovery.py — monthly full-text sweep<br/>helpers: queries.py, windows.py"]
        REG["registry.py — CIK-to-slug registry<br/>merger map: data/cik-mergers.csv"]
        ACQ["acquisition.py — classify and download docs<br/>helper: manifest.py"]
        DONE["done_marker.py — completion marker"]
        DRV -->|"step 1"| DISC
        DRV -->|"step 2"| REG
        DRV -->|"step 3"| ACQ
        DRV -->|"step 4"| DONE
    end

    subgraph SE["scripts/sec_edgar/ — shared EDGAR client layer"]

    ACQ --> TREE["data/tra-mentions/slug_cik/accession/<br/>primary docs + TRA-matched EX-10s"]
    DONE --> DM["data/tra-mentions/.phase1-done"]

    TREE --> P23["Phases 2 and 3 — per-firm reading,<br/>cross-firm consolidation<br/>(agent skills, not yet implemented)"]

    style P1 fill:#eef3fa,stroke:#7a92b8
    style SE fill:#eef3fa,stroke:#7a92b8

```

Not shown above:

- `scripts/find_candidates.py` and `scripts/pull_exhibits.py` — the
  exploratory sweep-and-download pair that `phase1_discovery` was built
  from; superseded, kept until the deferred-cleanup pass removes them.
- `scripts/tra_download.py` — the per-CIK downloader behind the
  `tra-download-filings` skill; overlaps with `phase1_discovery` and
  will be retired with the skill refactor.
- `scripts/tra_master_cik_list*.py`, `tra_form_distribution.py`,
  `tra_body_vs_exhibit.py`, `tra_refined_master.py` — one-off
  cache-only diagnostics from the May 2026 exploration; superseded.
- `scripts/legacy/` — retired code.
- `scripts/render_html.py` — dev utility for verifying
  browser-rendered HTML (mermaid, KaTeX), not part of the pipeline.

# Order of skill / script invocation

The mapping from phases to project skills and scripts. Skill design and
exact script names may evolve; the conceptual order does not.

| Phase | Skill or script | Output |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1\. Discovery and acquisition | `scripts/phase1_discovery/` (queries EDGAR for TRA-mentioning filings, groups by CIK, downloads primary docs alongside TRA-mentioning EX-10s). | `data/tra-mentions/` populated: per-firm document tree, `discovery.parquet`, `manifest.parquet`, `.phase1-done`. |
| 2\. Per-firm reading | A new per-firm reading skill that operates on one firm-slug directory at a time. | One `filing-log.md` per firm. |
| 3\. Cross-firm consolidation | An aggregation script that reads every `filing-log.md` and produces a contract-level index. | TRA index. |
| 4a. HTML-to-markdown | `tra-htm-to-md` (converts TRA contract HTML to clean markdown for the human-readable timelines). | `.md` companion files for each contract. |
| 4b. Per-firm timelines | A timeline-build script that consumes firm logs and contract-level index. | Per-firm timeline files. |
| 4c. Per-TRA timelines | A timeline-build script that consumes the contract-level index. | Per-TRA timeline files. |
| 4d. Database tables | `scripts/build_tra_database.py` (emits the structured tables; `scripts/build_dashboard.py` renders them as an HTML dashboard). | TRA, events, and firm-TRA-roles tables; dashboard. |
| 5\. Refresh | A `tra-refresh` skill that orchestrates incremental re-runs of Phases 1 through 4. | Updated database state. |

# Out of scope for this document

This document is the conceptual end state. It does not specify:

- File formats, library choices, or data-engineering details. Those
  decisions live in the individual skill specifications.
- How the reading agent prompts are written, or what its decision rule
  is. Section 11 of `tra-background.md` carries the substance-over-form
  classification rule that the agent must apply.
- The exact CIK seed methodology, sampling decisions, or rate-limiting
  rules. Those live in the discovery and download skill specifications.
- Quality-assurance steps, manual-review interfaces, or how
  disagreements between the agent and a human reviewer are handled.
  Those belong in a separate quality-control document.

The goal here is to make the end-to-end flow legible so that every
implementation choice can be evaluated against whether it serves this
flow.
